title: “At even my wife died” — the Brenton Greek does not mention her death
summary: The KJV says Ezekiel spoke to the people in the morning and “at even my wife died”. The Hebrew prints וַתָּמָת אִשְׁתִּי בָּעָרֶב, “and my wife died in the evening”. Brenton’s Greek of the verse says only that he spoke “as he commanded me in the evening”, and does not mention a wife or a death.
text: KJV Ezekiel 24:18: “So I spake unto the people in the morning: and at even my wife died; and I did in the morning as I was commanded.” Hebrew (WLC) Ezekiel 24:18: וָאֲדַבֵּ֤ר אֶל־הָעָם֙ בַּבֹּ֔קֶר וַתָּ֥מָת אִשְׁתִּ֖י בָּעָ֑רֶב וָאַ֥עַשׂ בַּבֹּ֖קֶר כַּאֲשֶׁ֥ר צֻוֵּֽיתִי׃ [and I spoke to the people in the morning, and my wife died in the evening, and I did in the morning as I was commanded]. Septuagint (Brenton Greek) Ezekiel 24:18: Καὶ ἐλάλησα πρὸς τὸν λαὸν τοπρωῒ, ὃν τρόπον ἐνετείλατὸ μοι ἑσπέρας, καὶ ἐποίησα τοπρωῒ, ὃν τρόπον ἐπετάγη μοι. Brenton English Ezekiel 24:18: “And I spoke to the people in the morning, as he commanded me in the evening, and I did in the morning as it was commanded me.” Fetched from https://ebible.org/eng-kjv/EZK24.htm, https://bolls.life/get-text/WLC/26/24/, https://ebible.org/grcbrent/EZK24.htm and https://ebible.org/eng-Brenton/EZK24.htm.
reasoning: The Hebrew has a finite clause with the verb for dying and the noun for wife. The Brenton Greek of 24:18 has no verb for dying and no noun for wife; the evening is there as the time of the command. The sign of 24:16 to 24:24 (the loss of the desire of the eyes, no mourning) is told in the KJV and Hebrew with the wife’s death stated in 24:18; in the Greek the verse leaves it unstated.
scope: T applies at Ezekiel 24:18, Septuagint only. The KJV agrees with the Hebrew. The record compares what one Greek page prints and does not claim every Greek witness omits the clause, say which text is original, or call the KJV wrong. title: “A conspiracy of her prophets” — the Brenton Greek says her princes
summary: The KJV says “There is a conspiracy of her prophets in the midst thereof, like a roaring lion”. The Hebrew prints קֶשֶׁר נְבִיאֶיהָ, “conspiracy of her prophets”. Brenton’s Greek prints οἱ ἀφηγούμενοι, “those who lead”, which Brenton’s English renders “princes”.

Brenton English Ezekiel 22:25: “whose princes in the midst of her are as roaring lions seizing prey, devouring souls by oppression, and taking bribes; and thy widows are multiplied in the midst of thee.” Fetched from https://ebible.org/eng-kjv/EZK22.htm, https://bolls.life/get-text/WLC/26/22/, https://ebible.org/grcbrent/EZK22.htm and https://ebible.org/eng-Brenton/EZK22.htm.

title: “The twelfth year … the tenth month” — the Brenton Greek says the tenth year, the twelfth month
summary: The KJV dates the arrival of the escaped man “in the twelfth year of our captivity, in the tenth month, in the fifth day”. The Hebrew prints בִּשְׁתֵּי עֶשְׂרֵה שָׁנָה בָּעֲשִׂרִי, twelfth year, in the tenth. Brenton’s Greek prints ἐν τῷ δεκάτῳ ἔτει, ἐν τῷ δωδεκάτῳ μηνί, tenth year, in the twelfth month. The day, the fifth, agrees.
text: KJV Ezekiel 33:21: “And it came to pass in the twelfth year of our captivity, in the tenth month, in the fifth day of the month, that one that had escaped out of Jerusalem came unto me, saying, The city is smitten.” Hebrew (WLC) Ezekiel 33:21: וַיְהִ֞י בִּשְׁתֵּ֧י עֶשְׂרֵ֣ה שָׁנָ֗ה בָּעֲשִׂרִ֛י בַּחֲמִשָּׁ֥ה לַחֹ֖דֶשׁ לְגָלוּתֵ֑נוּ בָּא־אֵלַ֨י הַפָּלִ֧יט מִירוּשָׁלִַ֛ם לֵאמֹ֖ר הֻכְּתָ֥ה הָעִֽיר׃ [and it happened in the twelfth year, in the tenth, on the fifth of the month of our exile, the escapee came to me from Jerusalem, saying, The city has been struck down]. Septuagint (Brenton Greek) Ezekiel 33:21: Καὶ ἐγενήθη ἐν τῷ δεκάτῳ ἔτει, ἐν τῷ δωδεκάτῳ μηνὶ, πέμπτῃ τοῦ μηνὸς τῆς αἰχμαλωσίας ἡμῶν, ἦλθε πρὸς μὲ ὁ ἀνασωθεὶς ἀπὸ Ἱερουσαλὴμ, λέγων, ἑάλω ἡ πόλις. Brenton English Ezekiel 33:21: “And it came to pass in the tenth year of our captivity, in the twelfth month, on the fifth day of the month, that one that had escaped from Jerusalem came to me, saying, The city is taken.” Fetched from https://ebible.org/eng-kjv/EZK33.htm, https://bolls.life/get-text/WLC/26/33/, https://ebible.org/grcbrent/EZK33.htm and https://ebible.org/eng-Brenton/EZK33.htm.
reasoning: The year and the month trade their numbers: the Hebrew has year 12 and month 10, the Greek year 10 and month 12. A reader of the two texts gets a different date for the news of Jerusalem’s fall.

title: Waters “to the ankles … to the knees” — the Brenton Greek has no ankles and says thighs
summary: In the vision of the river from the temple the KJV measures the depth four times: ankles (47:3), knees, loins (47:4) and a river to swim in (47:5). The Hebrew prints מֵי אַפְסָיִם, “waters of the ankles”, then מַיִם בִּרְכָּיִם, “waters, knees”, then מֵי מָתְנָיִם, “waters of the loins”. Brenton’s Greek prints ὕδωρ ἀφέσεως (“water of release”), then ἕως τῶν μηρῶν, “up to the thighs”, then ἕως ὀσφύος, “up to the loins”.
text: KJV Ezekiel 47:3: “And when the man that had the line in his hand went forth eastward, he measured a thousand cubits, and he brought me through the waters; the waters were to the ankles.” Hebrew (WLC) Ezekiel 47:3: בְּצֵאת־הָאִ֥ישׁ קָדִ֖ים וְקָ֣ו בְּיָדֹ֑ו וַיָּ֤מָד אֶ֙לֶף֙ בָּֽאַמָּ֔ה וַיַּעֲבִרֵ֥נִי בַמַּ֖יִם מֵ֥י אָפְסָֽיִם׃ [and the man went out eastward with a line in his hand and measured a thousand by the cubit, and he brought me through the water, water of ankles]. Septuagint (Brenton Greek) Ezekiel 47:3: καθὼς ἔξοδος ἀνδρὸς ἐξεναντίας· καὶ μέτρον ἐν τῇ χειρὶ αὐτοῦ· καὶ διεμέτρησε χιλίους ἐν τῷ μετρῳ, καὶ διῆλθεν ἐν τῷ ὕδατι ὕδωρ ἀφέσεως· Brenton English Ezekiel 47:3: “in the direction in which a man went forth opposite; and there was a measuring line in his hand, and he measured a thousand cubits with the measure;” KJV Ezekiel 47:4: “Again he measured a thousand, and brought me through the waters; the waters were to the knees. Again he measured a thousand, and brought me through; the waters were to the loins.” Hebrew (WLC) Ezekiel 47:4: וַיָּ֣מָד אֶ֔לֶף וַיַּעֲבִרֵ֥נִי בַמַּ֖יִם מַ֣יִם בִּרְכָּ֑יִם וַיָּ֣מָד אֶ֔לֶף וַיַּעֲבִרֵ֖נִי מֵ֥י מָתְנָֽיִם׃ [and he measured a thousand and brought me through the water, water of knees; and he measured a thousand and brought me through, water of loins]. Septuagint (Brenton Greek) Ezekiel 47:4: καὶ διεμέτρησε χιλίους, καὶ διῆλθεν ἐν τῷ ὕδατι ὕδωρ ἕως τῶν μηρῶν· καὶ διεμέτρησε χιλίους, καὶ διῆλθεν ὕδωρ ἕως ὀσφύος. Brenton English Ezekiel 47:4: “and he passed through the water; it was water of a fountain: and again he measured a thousand, and passed through the water; and the water was up to the thighs: and again he measured a thousand; and he passed through water up to the loins.” Fetched from https://ebible.org/eng-kjv/EZK47.htm, https://bolls.life/get-text/WLC/26/47/, https://ebible.org/grcbrent/EZK47.htm and https://ebible.org/eng-Brenton/EZK47.htm.
reasoning: The KJV has ankles, knees, loins. The Hebrew has the same three body parts. The Brenton Greek has a first depth that is not a body part, then thighs, then loins; Brenton’s English prints “water of a fountain” for it at 47:4. title: The wall measured “five hundred reeds” on each side — the Brenton Greek has cubits and a different order of sides
summary: In the vision of the temple the KJV measures each side of the outer wall at “five hundred reeds, with the measuring reed”, taking the sides east, north, south, west. The Hebrew prints חֲמֵשׁ מֵאוֹת קָנִים, five hundred reeds, in the order east, north, south, west. Brenton’s Greek prints πεντακοσίους, five hundred, with πήχεις, cubits, at 42:17, and takes the sides east, north, west (θάλασσαν), south (Νότον).
text: KJV Ezekiel 42:16: “He measured the east side with the measuring reed, five hundred reeds, with the measuring reed round about.” Hebrew (WLC) Ezekiel 42:16: מָדַ֛ד ר֥וּחַ הַקָּדִ֖ים בִּקְנֵ֣ה הַמִּדָּ֑ה חֲמֵשׁ־ [אֵמֹות כ] (מֵאֹ֥ות ק) קָנִ֛ים בִּקְנֵ֥ה הַמִּדָּ֖ה סָבִֽיב׃ [he measured the east side with the measuring reed, five hundred reeds, with the measuring reed round about]. Septuagint (Brenton Greek) Ezekiel 42:16: Καὶ ἔστη κατὰ νώτου τῆς πύλης τῆς βλεπούσης κατὰ ἀνατολὰς, καὶ διεμέτρησε πεντακοσίους ἐν τῷ καλάμῳ τοῦ μέτρου. Brenton English Ezekiel 42:16: “And he stood behind the gate looking eastward, and measured five hundred cubits with the measuring reed.” KJV Ezekiel 42:17: “He measured the north side, five hundred reeds, with the measuring reed round about.” Hebrew (WLC) Ezekiel 42:17: מָדַ֖ד ר֣וּחַ הַצָּפֹ֑ון חֲמֵשׁ־מֵאֹ֥ות קָנִ֛ים בִּקְנֵ֥ה הַמִּדָּ֖ה סָבִֽיב׃ [he measured the north side, five hundred reeds]. Septuagint (Brenton Greek) Ezekiel 42:17: Καὶ ἐπέστρεψε πρὸς Βοῤῥᾶν, καὶ διεμέτρησε τὸ κατὰ πρόσωπον τοῦ Βοῤῥᾶ, πήχεις πεντακοσίους ἐν τῷ καλάμῳ τοῦ μέτρου. Brenton English Ezekiel 42:17: “And he turned to the north and measured in front of the north side five hundred cubits with the measuring reed.” KJV Ezekiel 42:18: “He measured the south side, five hundred reeds, with the measuring reed.” Hebrew (WLC) Ezekiel 42:18: אֵ֛ת ר֥וּחַ הַדָּרֹ֖ום מָדָ֑ד חֲמֵשׁ־מֵאֹ֥ות קָנִ֖ים בִּקְנֵ֥ה הַמִּדָּֽה׃ [he measured the south side, five hundred reeds]. Septuagint (Brenton Greek) Ezekiel 42:18: Καὶ ἐπέστρεψε πρὸς θάλασσαν, καὶ διεμέτρησε τὸ κατὰ πρόσωπον θαλάσσης, πεντακοσίους ἐν τῷ καλάμῳ τοῦ μέτρου. Brenton English Ezekiel 42:18: “And he turned to the west, and measured in front of the west side, five hundred cubits with the measuring reed.” KJV Ezekiel 42:19: “He turned about to the west side, and measured five hundred reeds with the measuring reed.” Hebrew (WLC) Ezekiel 42:19: סָבַ֖ב אֶל־ר֣וּחַ הַיָּ֑ם מָדַ֛ד חֲמֵשׁ־מֵאֹ֥ות קָנִ֖ים בִּקְנֵ֥ה הַמִּדָּֽה׃ [he turned about to the west side, five hundred reeds]. title: Ezekiel bears his baggage “upon thy shoulders” — the Brenton Greek has him lifted up on others’ shoulders
summary: In the sign of the exile the KJV has Ezekiel carry his baggage on his own shoulder through the hole in the wall (12:6, 12:7). The Hebrew prints עַל־כָּתֵף תִּשָּׂא, “on a shoulder you shall carry”, and עַל־כָּתֵף נָשָׂאתִי, “on a shoulder I carried”. Brenton’s Greek prints ἐπʼ ὤμων ἀναληφθήσῃ, “thou shalt be taken up on shoulders”, and ἐπʼ ὤμων ἀνελήφθην, “I was taken up on shoulders”.

title: “Telabib” and “astonished” — the Brenton Greek has neither

The Hebrew prints וְנָתַתִּי צְבִי בְּאֶרֶץ חַיִּים, “and I will give beauty in the land of the living”. Brenton’s Greek prints μηδὲ ἀναστῇς ἐπὶ γῆς ζωῆς, “nor [that thou] rise upon the land of life”, which is a further negative aim of the same sentence.
text: KJV Ezekiel 26:20: “When I shall bring thee down with them that descend into the pit, with the people of old time, and shall set thee in the low parts of the earth, in places desolate of old, with them that go down to the pit, that thou be not inhabited; and I shall set glory in the land of the living;” Hebrew (WLC) Ezekiel 26:20: וְהֹורַדְתִּיךְ֩ אֶת־יֹ֨ורְדֵי בֹ֜ור אֶל־עַ֣ם עֹולָ֗ם וְ֠הֹושַׁבְתִּיךְ בְּאֶ֨רֶץ תַּחְתִּיֹּ֜ות כָּחֳרָבֹ֤ות מֵֽעֹולָם֙ אֶת־יֹ֣ורְדֵי בֹ֔ור לְמַ֖עַן לֹ֣א תֵשֵׁ֑בִי וְנָתַתִּ֥י צְבִ֖י בְּאֶ֥רֶץ חַיִּֽים׃ [and I will bring you down with those who go down to the pit, to the people of old, and make you dwell in the lower parts of the earth, like the ruins of old, with those who go down to the pit, so that you will not be inhabited; and I will give beauty in the land of the living]. Septuagint (Brenton Greek) Ezekiel 26:20: καὶ καταβιβάσω σε πρὸς τοὺς καταβαίνοντας εἰς βόθρον πρὸς λαὸν αἰῶνος, καὶ κατοικιῶ σε εἰς βάθη τῆς γῆς ὡς ἔρημον αἰώνιον μετὰ καταβαινόντων εἰς βόθρον, ὅπως μὴ κατοικηθῇς, μηδὲ ἀναστῇς ἐπὶ γῆς ζωῆς, Brenton English Ezekiel 26:20: “and great waters shall cover thee; and I shall bring thee down to them that go down to the pit, to the people of old time, and shall cause thee to dwell in the depths of the earth, as in everlasting desolation, with them that go down to the pit, that thou mayest not be inhabited, nor stand upon the land of life;” Fetched from https://ebible.org/eng-kjv/EZK26.htm, https://bolls.life/get-text/WLC/26/26/, https://ebible.org/grcbrent/EZK26.htm and https://ebible.org/eng-Brenton/EZK26.htm.
reasoning: The Hebrew clause is a statement by the speaker with a new verb, “I will give”, and a noun, “beauty” or “glory”. The Greek clause is a continuation of the purpose clause “that thou mayest not be inhabited”, with a negative and a verb meaning to stand or rise, addressed to Tyre. The KJV has God setting glory in the land of the living; the Greek has Tyre not standing in it.
scope: T applies at Ezekiel 26:20, Septuagint only. The KJV agrees with the Hebrew. The record compares what each text prints. It does not decide which is original, does not identify the land of the living or whose glory is meant, and does not claim an error in either text; the Hebrew noun צְבִי is not rendered or defined here beyond the KJV’s own “glory”. The Hebrew quoted is the Westminster Leningrad Codex digital text. A digital named edition is not proof that every manuscript agrees; other Hebrew manuscripts were not examined. The Greek is Brenton’s printed edition of the Septuagint, an ancient Greek translation tradition of the Old Testament. It is not a critical apparatus and does not show that all Greek witnesses agree or which reading is original. title: “Him that passeth out and him that returneth” — the Brenton Greek has men and cattle

reasoning: The Hebrew has two participles for coming and going. The Greek has two nouns, people and livestock, and no verbs of travel. The same Hebrew pair is read in the KJV as travellers; the Greek turns it into the inhabitants of the land, human and animal.
